Interesting — I requested 11 DOWNs, but only 6 were executed (step 8 → 14). The batch was cut off partway through? "The code executed 6 actions in the previous sequence." Hmm, maybe the environment limits the number of actions per call, or maybe the frame returned after 6 actions. Current state: black is at rows 30-38, columns 27-35; charcoal is visible at rows 33-38, columns 27-29 (overlapping). The timer is currently 13 pixels (node 3 B 13: rows 0-12, column 63). Wait, the timer is decreasing faster: it was about 56 before, and now it's 13? Let me count: steps so far: 1 RIGHT, 2 LEFT, 3 UP, 4 SPACE, 5 ACTION7, 6-8 3 RIGHTs, 9-14 6 DOWNs = 13 actions, timer 64-13=51? But node 3 shows 13 pixels at rows 0-12 — so the timer has 13 pixels left?? That means it decreased by 51 in 13 actions? No wait — node 3 is the black portion of the right-edge bar (rows 0-12, column 63, 13 pixels), and node 4 is the yellow portion (rows 13-63, 51 pixels). So the right-edge bar is: top 13 pixels black, bottom 51 pixels yellow. The black portion is growing from the top! So the timer bar is being filled with black from the top — the yellow portion is shrinking. The yellow portion was originally 64; now it's 51. So 13 actions consumed 13. OK, consistent: timer = 51 remaining.
So the batch of 11 DOWNs only executed 6. Why? Maybe there's a per-call limit, or the action list got truncated. The message says "executed 6 actions." Probably the environment caps it at 6 per call. I need to batch in smaller chunks (6 or fewer).
Current position: black/charcoal are at rows 30-38, columns 27-35. The yellow target is at rows 45-53, columns 51-59.
Remaining for hypothesis A (charcoal onto yellow): +15 rows (5 DOWNs), +24 columns (8 LEFTs). Total 13 actions. Timer 51. OK.
